newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Portugal rate cut.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Portugal rate cut.

text.p: The following views were expressed by analysts and economists after the Bank of Portugal cut its repurchase pact rate and its draining and emergency rates by 20 basis points.
The repo rate stands at 6.70 percent, with the draining rate at 6.20 percent and the emergency lending at 8.30 percent.
ISABEL CABRAL, analyst at Lisbon brokers Fincor

"The repo cut was as expected but the draining rate cut was a bit of a surprise. It could signal that the Bank of Portugal could cut the repo again at the start of 1997. The cut in the draining rate is a pretty positive sign for the markets because by keeping the spread between the two (the draining rate and the repo), if inflation allows, one could look for fresh cuts in the repo."
JOAO MIGUEL LOURENCO of brokers Siemca

"It was a surprise. We were not expecting any changes because of the disappointing inflation (for November) and the relatively high level of the (public sector) wage deal which was three percent. It seems to me that the determining factor was the cut in Spain. But as the market was expecting it, I don't expect a big (market) reaction.
"I am very sceptical (about further cuts). I don't see any before we have fresh information on inflation."
"It should not have much impact on the market because it was discounted. But the decision to cut the drain rate could be a signal of further cuts (in the repo) to come."
